title: Stage removal of compatibility shims and coordinate staggered SDK bumps
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Background: Over the last 18 months we have accumulated compatibility shims and optional fields across the Python, JS, and Go SDKs to smooth customer migrations and preserve backwards compatibility. These shims increase maintenance burden, prevent kernel-level optimizations from being exercised cleanly, and create a confusing API surface for developers.

Goal: Remove selected backward-compatibility shims and deprecated optional parameters from SDKs in a staged, low-risk way while coordinating dependency bumps (http client, serialization libs, and gRPC/transport layers). Deliverables: migration guides for each language, canary releases for customers on Dedicated, CI perf/regression gates, and automated codemods for common callsites.
acceptance_criteria:
- All three language SDKs (python, js, go) released with target dependency bumps and deprecation warnings removed behind flags.
- Migration guides published in docs.redwood.ai and linked from SDK READMEs.
- Performance benchmark (token/sec) parity or improvement in base CI jobs; no >5% regression allowed.
- No customer-facing errors in the canary cohort for 72 hours.
- Automated lint/codemod applied to internal example repos and sample apps.
implementation_plan:
1) Identify concrete shim set: list optional params, headers, and legacy response fields to remove. 2) Create feature flags in each SDK to toggle 'compat-mode' (default on) — release initial SDKs with new deps and compat-mode. 3) Run integration tests against Hosted, Dedicated, and Private stacks. 4) Flip compat-mode for internal canary customers and monitoring dashboards. 5) After 2 weeks of canary, cut GA without compat-mode and ship migration docs and codemods. 6) Post-release follow-up: collect error telemetry and rollback plan.

Subtasks:
- Python: bump httpx -> 0.26, protobuf -> 4.x compatibility check, remove optional 'legacy_meta' param.
- JS: bump node-fetch -> undici or native fetch, roll patch for ESM/CJS interop, strip old 'responseEnvelope' option.
- Go: bump grpc-go to 1.62, tidy module replacements, remove legacy unstructured marshal path.
- CI: add perf/regression tests and baseline snapshots.
- Docs: migration guide + changelog + sample codemods (python ast, jscodeshift, gofmt script).
testing_notes:
- Add smoke tests for each SDK that exercise generation, streaming, embeddings, and function/tool calling after deps bumps.
- Run perf harness on representative prompt sets (chat and long-context generation).
- Use canary customer telemetry dashboard and set alert for error rate >0.5% or latency 2x baseline.
- Create unit tests for new flag behavior and ensure flags respected when serializing older fields.
rollout_plan:
Week 0: branch and PRs prepared for all three SDKs + internal docs.
Week 1: Release alpha packages with compat-mode default on; invite 5 internal customers for early canary.
Week 2: Flip compat-mode for internal canary subset; monitor.
Week 3: Expand canary to Dedicated customers (opt-in); continue monitoring.
Week 4: GA cut with compat-mode removed and docs published.
Fallback: revert packages or re-enable compat-mode if we observe spikes in errors or >5% perf regressions.
blockers:
- Final confirmation from API/Platform about timeline for deprecating legacy response fields.
- One critical dependency has a breaking change on Go modules (we are waiting on downstream patch).
- Need QA perf budget/time on the shared perf harness cluster.
